chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me who said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan Al-Farsi, from Al-Sulayman ibn Ja'far Al-Ja'fari, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, from his father, from Zayd, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) passed by a group of people and asked them: 'On what have you gathered?' They said: 'O Messenger of God, this is an insane epileptic, so we have gathered around him.' He said: 'This one is not insane, but he is the afflicted.' Then he said: 'Shall I inform you of the true insane one?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of God.' He said: '[Indeed, the true insane one is] the one who walks with pride, looks from the corners of his eyes, shakes his sides with his shoulders, wishes for God's Paradise while he disobeys Him, from whom his evil is not guarded, and from whom goodness is not hoped for. That is the insane one, and this one is merely afflicted.'

key_terms.الْمُتَبَخْتِرُ: the one who walks with pride/haughtiness
key_terms.لَا يُؤْمَنُ شَرُّهُ: whose evil is not guarded against

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of a truly insane person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to distinguish between physiological affliction and spiritual delusion, a key concept in Shia ethical theology. The 'true insane' person is defined not by loss of reason, but by the dissonance between their claim to Paradise and their actual disobedience, characterized by arrogant demeanor (*tabakhkur*) and uncertainty of their good deeds. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *amal* (action) and *khuluq* (character) as indicators of spiritual health.
